title: Pseudo-coherent derived evaluation isomorphism
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that $L$ is bounded below in the derived category, i.e. $L\in D^+(R)$, meaning $H^i(L)=0$ for all $i\ll0$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and that $M$ has finite injective dimension (isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $R$-modules) [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the canonical derived evaluation morphism of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map]
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above complex $P$ of finite free $R$-modules representing $K$, by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and an integer $u$ with $P^s=0$ for $s>u$. The finite-injective-dimension hypothesis, in the explicit meaning given in the statement, supplies a bounded complex of injective modules $I$ representing $M$; fix $a\le b$ with $I^p=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives] the abelian category of $R$-modules has enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to $L\in D^+(R)$ to obtain a bounded-below complex of injectives $J$ representing $L$, with $J^j=0$ for $j<\ell$. Both $I$ and $J$ are K-injective by the bounded-below-injective assertion of that same node. All bounds are bounds on terms of these chosen complexes, not just on their cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0A68, proof, choices of representatives; derived.tex Tags 013K and 070J

proof.text: Each $P^s$ is flat: after choosing a finite basis, tensoring with $P^s$ is a finite direct sum of the identity functor on modules, and hence preserves exact sequences componentwise. Consequently [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P$ K-flat. Use the equivalent quasi-isomorphism criterion of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] to express this in the categorical K-flat convention. Then [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], together with the symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$, computes $R\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ by $T=\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)$, where $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(J,I)$. No K-flatness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; Tag 0A68, displayed total tensor model

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-double-evaluation-signed-derived-model] to these $P,J,I$. It provides $A=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J)$, $B=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(A,I)$ and a chain map $E:T\to B$, with $E(g\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{|f||x|}g(f(x))$. Its derived comparisons identify $Q(E)$ with the specified canonical evaluation. Its K-flat and K-injective hypotheses were verified in Steps 1--2.

All term bounds and finite-freeness required by [lem-trf-double-evaluation-finite-components] hold for these representatives. It makes each $E^n$ invertible: its coefficient $(-1)^{s(r+1)}$ agrees with Step 3 because $k=|f|=-r-s$ gives $ks\equiv s(r+1)\pmod2$.

source.place: Tag 0A68, case (2), finite-support and component invertibility

proof.text: From $d_BE=Ed_T$, multiplication in consecutive degrees by the component inverses gives $E^{-1}d_B=d_TE^{-1}$. Thus the component inverses form an inverse chain map. The localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves that inverse, so $Q(E)$ is invertible. Step 3 identifies it with $e_{QP,QJ,QI}$. The representative isomorphisms $QP\cong K$, $QJ\cong L$ and $QI\cong M$ of Step 1, together with the naturality of the canonical morphism of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map] (covariant in $K,M$, contravariant in $L$), conjugate $e_{QP,QJ,QI}$ to $e_{K,L,M}$ by isomorphisms, so $e_{K,L,M}$ is an isomorphism.
